div.head: Af 36.2[a]
div.ab: gif se ord sy þreo fingre ufor þonne hindeweard sceaft.
gif se ord sie ufor þonne hindeweard sceaft.
si acutum lancee sit altius tribus digitis quam cuspis.
gif se ord sie ufor þonne hindeweard sceaft.
if the point is higher than the shaft in the back.
supposing the point to be higher than the [other] end of the shaft, by the width of three fingers.
if the point is higher than the butt end of the shaft. If they are both level, the point and the butt end, that is to be [considered] without risk.
vorausgesetzt, die Spitze sei (3 Finger) höher als hinterer Schaft.
provided that the point is (3 fingers) higher than the rear shaft.
div.note: Textus RoJJetisis and Quadripartitus add here: “three fingers”
Whitelock translates Af 36.2 as one clause, which the sheet divides into rows 36.2[a], 36.2[b]; her translation of the whole is given here, in the first row.
